name: J. M. Hannaford
role: General freight agent of the Northern Pacific
bio: J. M. Hannaford was the Northern Pacific's general freight agent. In July 1884 his word that freight cars need not be unloaded until fall figured in the Cow Boy's quarrel over a Medora freight house, and in July 1885 he reported 98,000 cattle shipped west over the road the year before.
